doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: First recordings: Japanese date, India Navigation and Contemporary
summary: He recorded three albums within months, in Chicago for a Japanese label, for India Navigation, and for Contemporary with Elvin Jones.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: When was the first time you got to record?

That’s kind of interesting. I kind of recorded three albums almost simultaneously. It was a little unusual. The ACAM, which is the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians, had garnered some attention from the Japanese in Chicago, and there were some Japanese record companies that were coming over and recording a lot of that, Muhal was doing records and Henry and everyone. And they had caught, I had caught their eye as well. And there was a guy, he came over, and I was in New York. Actually when I left Brazil I came to New York and I actually never went back to Chicago. So by this time I was in New York. And while I was in New York I also met a guy named Robert Cummins, who had a record company called India Navigation. And I had caught his eye. So I actually, I think, if I get this right, I think the first record that, the Japanese fella, his name was Mahasico Eu came and we had a little bit of a language problem. And he thought that I would like to go to Chicago and make this record. And I thought he wanted to go to Chicago, when both of us would have preferred to stay in New York. And needless to say we ended up in Chicago. So I made the record there. And I think that was the very first one I did actually in the studio and recorded. I came back to New York. Then the next one I did I think was the India Navigation record, I think. But that was not the first — the India Navigation I think was the first one released maybe. I’m not sure about this, because it’s a little bit fuzzy. But the reason I said there were three because after that I had joined Elvin Jones’ band. So I was on tour with Elvin Jones and Elvin did the surprise and when I got to California he said, “I’ve got a record date for you.” And I was surprised. He had secured a recording for me, it was under my own name and he was on the record. And that was for the Great Contemporary, Lester Koenig. So I did that record. And I’m trying to remember which was actually the first one that was released, which most people would think of as my first record, in terms of — but they were all recorded just about in the same time. I mean, within a month or two apart. So to tell you the truth I don’t really remember which is actually the first one or the second. But those three came pretty close together.
